No SRU upload for resolute, the only series where the bug reproduces, is evident. The fix landed only in the development release (tenacious), and the resolute debdiffs have not been sponsored or accepted into resolute-proposed. The fix was released in 1.9.1-0.1ubuntu4 for tenacious, which links against libcrypto.so.4 and cannot be installed on 26.04.

The reviewer flagged the packaging nit 'Origin: backport' in the patch Jorge authored, which should be 'Origin: upstream'. It is marked as a blocker, and no later comment shows it was fixed. Patch ordering in d/p/series and use of full commit hashes were also raised, and the patches' dependency order has not been confirmed.

The test plan is not reproducible as written. The reviewer's run of the reproducer script failed early because tpm2-abrmd did not become ready on resolute, and it lacks the apt install line for dependencies. It also does not say how to verify that the fix does not regress behaviour in stonking, where OpenSSL 4 has no engine support.

The reviewer asked for the upstream OpenSSL change that caused the regression in 3.0.14, in order to rule out Noble and Jammy (which have OpenSSL 3.0.x with engine support), and for a rationale for including the patches in stonking, where they are essentially no-ops. There is no reply to either request.
The reviewer asked for a PPA build with the patches so that others can test and review the packages. None has been linked.

A user reported that after the engine loads a TPM key once, libtss2-esys cannot create RSA keys in the same process (EVP_PKEY_fromdata_init returns -2), and that re-authentication may fail until wpa_supplicant is restarted. The user later called this an unverified LLM hypothesis and has not tested repeated connections, so a possible residual or regression issue after the patch has not been ruled out.

The Impact section has not been updated to explain that wpa_supplicant in resolute registers an OpenSSL ENGINE as the RSA EVP_PKEY_METHOD, and that engines are not supported in OpenSSL 4 (stonking), which was requested by the reviewer.

comments.author: whershberger
comments.body:
There are two standing issues with these patches:

- get_global_pool_hard_max_size parses /proc/sys/vm/max_map_count incorrectly, resulting in the default value being used unconditionally
- The default value returned by get_global_pool_hard_max_size is UINT_MAX; a better/conservative choice would be the kernel's default max_map_count (65530)

We've submitted upstream patches to resolve both of these issues; neither have been merged to qemu's master yet.

https://lists.gnu.org/archive/html/qemu-devel/2026-10/msg04337.html
